hints: Focus on what combustion products tell you, all the carbon ends up in $\text{CO}_2$ and all the hydrogen ends up in $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
Work out moles of $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ first, remember $0.132/44 = 0.003$ mol and $0.054/18 = 0.003$ mol.
Double the moles of water to get moles of H atoms, find the simplest C to H ratio, then check which alkenes match that empirical formula.
walkthrough:
**Find moles of C and H from products**

All C in the hydrocarbon forms $\text{CO}_2$, and all H forms $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. So start with moles.

$$n = \frac{m}{M}$$

**Calculate moles of carbon dioxide**

$M_r$ of $\text{CO}_2 = 44$. This gives moles of C atoms directly.

$$n(\text{CO}_2) = \frac{0.132}{44} = 0.003 \text{ mol}$$ 
So $n(\text{C}) = 0.003 \text{ mol}$

**Calculate moles of hydrogen**

$M_r$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O} = 18$. But each water has 2 H atoms, so be careful.

$$n(\text{H}_2\text{O}) = \frac{0.054}{18} = 0.003 \text{ mol}$$
$$n(\text{H}) = 2 \times 0.003 = 0.006 \text{ mol}$$

**Get the empirical formula**

Divide by the smallest to get the whole number ratio.

$$\text{C} : \text{H} = 0.003 : 0.006 = 1 : 2$$
Empirical formula is $\text{CH}_2$.

**Check the three alkenes**

1: $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2$ is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$, which simplifies to $\text{CH}_2$.
2: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$ is $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6$, which simplifies to $\text{CH}_2$.
3: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3$ is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8$, which simplifies to $\text{CH}_2$.
All three fit, so 1, 2 and 3 are all possible.

options.A: Correct, because all three structures are alkenes with general formula $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}$ and empirical formula $\text{CH}_2$. This exactly matches the 1:2 C:H ratio found from the combustion data.
options.B: Incorrect. This would mean only 1 and 2 are correct. There is no reason to exclude 3, since but-2-ene ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_8$) also has a 1:2 ratio. Students choosing this often miscount H in structure 3.
options.C: Incorrect. This would mean only 2 and 3 are correct. Ethene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$) clearly also fits the $\text{CH}_2$ ratio, so 1 cannot be excluded.
options.D: Incorrect. This would mean only 1 is correct. Combustion analysis only gives the empirical formula, not the molecular mass, so any multiple of $\text{CH}_2$ that is a sensible hydrocarbon, including $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6$ and $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8$, is possible.
